question.text: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the minimum investment requirement between Mutual Funds, Portfolio Management Services (PMS), and Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs)?

answer.text: MF: Rs. 5,000 minimum; PMS: Rs. 25 lakh; AIF: Rs. 25 lakh
MF: Rs. 500 minimum; PMS: Rs. 50 lakh; AIF: Rs. 50 lakh
MF: Rs. 500 or as specified in the scheme; PMS: Rs. 50 lakh; AIF: Rs. 1 crore
MF: Rs. 1,000 minimum; PMS: Rs. 1 crore; AIF: Rs. 50 lakh

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series V-A workbook (p41), the minimum investment in a mutual fund scheme can be as low as Rs. 500 or such other amount as specified by the scheme. NISM PMS workbook (p94) sets the PMS minimum at Rs. 50 lakh, and NISM AIF workbook (p96-p98) sets the AIF minimum investment at Rs. 1 crore. The Trap: Option A uses the pre-2020 PMS minimum of Rs. 25 lakh, which has since been raised to Rs. 50 lakh. Option D incorrectly swaps the PMS and AIF minimums. Stating "no regulatory minimum" for MF lump sums is not the workbook position — the workbook anchors a Rs. 500 floor with scheme-specific overrides. Note: The hierarchy is MF (Rs. 500 / scheme-specified) → PMS (Rs. 50 lakh) → AIF (Rs. 1 crore), reflecting the rising sophistication and risk profile expected at each tier.
